slides.heading: Monotonic Array
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Monotonic Array, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Is the array entirely non-increasing or entirely non-decreasing?
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Is the array entirely non-increasing or entirely non-decreasing?

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: An array is monotonic if it never goes both up and down.
slides.narration: An array is monotonic if it never goes both up and down.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Naive: determine direction from the first unequal pair, then re-scan
Simpler: track two flags in one pass → O(n)
No sorting or extra memory needed
slides.narration: A common first attempt finds the direction from the first unequal pair, then checks everything again. Tracking two flags, can-still-be-increasing and can-still-be-decreasing, does it in a single pass.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Track two flags, non-increasing and non-decreasing
2. Clear the opposite flag on each rise or fall
3. Return true if either flag survives
slides.narration: Step by step. First, track two flags, non-increasing and non-decreasing. Second, clear the opposite flag on each rise or fall. Third, return true if either flag survives.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: -1 → -5: inc=False, dec=True
slides.narration: From -1 to -5: it drops, so the array can't be non-decreasing.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: -10 → -1100: inc=False, dec=True
slides.narration: From -10 to -1100: it drops, so the array can't be non-decreasing.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: -1100 → -1100: inc=False, dec=True
slides.narration: From -1100 to -1100: equal values don't break either direction.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: -1102 → -9001: inc=False, dec=True
slides.narration: From -1102 to -9001: it drops, so the array can't be non-decreasing.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We keep increasing and decreasing flags. Any drop clears increasing, any rise clears decreasing, and we return whether either survives.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Leading equal values before the trend
slides.narration: Empty and single-element arrays are monotonic, equal neighbours are fine, and leading equal values don't fix a direction prematurely.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Early exit when both flags are false
slides.narration: You can return early once both flags are false. A follow-up asks for strict monotonicity.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: An array is monotonic if it never goes both up and down.
slides.narration: To recap Monotonic Array: An array is monotonic if it never goes both up and down. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
